'''Paras Nath Prasad''' (born in 1946) is an Indian chemist. He is the SUNY Distinguished Professor at the [[University at Buffalo]] and holds a tenured faculty appointment in the department of Chemistry.  In addition, he also holds non-tenured appointments in Physics, Medicine, and Electrical Engineering at the [[University at Buffalo]] and serves as the executive director of the Institute for Lasers, Photonics and Biophotonics.

==Early life and education==
Prasad was born in 1946<ref>{{cite web |title=Paras Nath Prasad |url=https://library.buffalo.edu/archives/ubpeople/detail.html?ID=3116 |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021}}</ref> in [[Sitamarhi]], [[Bihar]].<ref name="Thomas">{{cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Karen |title=2016 SPIE Gold Medal |url=https://spie.org/news/spie-professional-magazine-archive/2016-july/paras-prasad-spie-gold-medal-fantastic-voyage?SSO=1 |publisher=SPIE |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=July 1, 2016}}</ref>  He obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree and [[Master's degree]] at the [[Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University]] and his PhD from the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Paras N. Prasad, PhD |url=https://arts-sciences.buffalo.edu/physics/faculty/paras-n-prasad.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref> His doctoral research was in the area of biophotonics.<ref name="Thomas"/>

==Career==
Prasad joined the faculty at the [[University at Buffalo]] (UB) in 1974. He has conducted research on two-photon technology and has served as Director of the Photonics Research Laboratory.<ref name="medal">{{cite web |last1=Danzig |first1=Joan |title=Prasad to Receive Schoellkopf Medal |url=https://publichealth.buffalo.edu/global-health/news-and-events/latest-news.host.html/content/shared/university/news/news-center-releases/1999/05/2764.detail.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 4, 2021 |date=May 11, 1999}}</ref> He has served as executive director of the Institute for Research in Lasers, Photonics and Biophotonics. Prasad has contributed to the development of photonic materials for biomedical applications including nanoshells containing various diagnostic and therapeutic agents <ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldbaum |first1=Ellen |title=Novel Photonic Material Developed At UB Reveals How Human Breast-Cancer Cell Takes Up Anticancer Agent |url=https://publichealth.buffalo.edu/global-health/news-and-events/latest-news.host.html/content/shared/university/news/news-center-releases/1999/09/4418.detail.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=September 27, 1999}}</ref><ref name="Thomas"/> He has published a book entitled "Nanophotonics,"."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldbaum |first1=Ellen |title=UB Professor Publishes the First Book on Nanophotonics, the Interaction of Light with Matter on the Nanoscale |url=https://publichealth.buffalo.edu/global-health/news-and-events/latest-news.host.html/content/shared/university/news/news-center-releases/2004/04/6667.detail.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=April 12, 2004}}</ref>

Prasad has contributed to research at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] by serving as an external advisor in two projects in biotechnology and nanotechnology. He was awarded an honorary doctorate by the institution in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hsu |first1=Charlotte |title=Prasad receives honorary doctorate from Sweden's Royal Institute of Technology |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2013/11/023.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=November 18, 2013}}</ref>

===Awards and honors===
He was elected a Fellow of the Optical Society in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paras N. Prasad {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Paras_N_Prasad |access-date=2024-09-18 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref> He received a 1997 [[John Simon Guggenheim Fellowship]] in Engineering.<ref>{{cite web |title=PARAS N. PRASAD |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/paras-n-prasad/ |publisher=Guggenheim Fellowship |access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref> He was named the Samuel P. Capen Professor of Chemistry and earned the 1999 Jacob F. Schoellkopf Medal from the [[American Chemical Society]] "for his outstanding achievements in spectroscopy and materials science specifically focused on photonics technology."<ref name="medal"/> He was elected a fellow of the [[International Society for Optical Engineering]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldbaum |first1=Ellen |title=Prasad Elected Fellow of International Society for Optical Engineering |url=https://publichealth.buffalo.edu/global-health/news-and-events/latest-news.host.html/content/shared/university/news/news-center-releases/2005/05/7314.detail.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=May 23, 2005}}</ref> and was named by [[Scientific American]] as one of the Scientific American 50 in 2005.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldbaum |first1=Ellen |title=Prasad Named One of World's Top 50 in Science |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2005/11/7626.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=November 7, 2005}}</ref> In 2003, he along with many other faculty were honored by the State University of New York."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wuetcher |first1=Sue |title=Prasad Receives Excellence Award from SUNY; 14 Other UB Faculty Members Recognized for Research Efforts |url=https://engineering.buffalo.edu/home/news/seas.host.html/content/shared/university/news/news-center-releases/2003/06/6266.detail.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=June 2, 2003}}</ref> He was named an honorary professor at [[Zhejiang University]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldbaum |first1=Ellen |title=Chinese university to honor Paras Prasad |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubreporter/archive/vol37/vol37n25/articles/PrasadAward.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=March 23, 2006}}</ref>

In 2014, Prasad received UB's first Innovation Impact Award in recognition of his work in "developing the use of magnetic and laser-activated nanoparticles for cancer diagnosis and treatment."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Andrei |first1=Michael |title=Prasad recognized with first UB Innovation Impact Award |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubnow/stories/2015/02/prasad_innovation_impact.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=February 26, 2015}}</ref> He received the UB President's Medal in recognition of extraordinary service to the university.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wuetcher |first1=Sue |title=Prasad, Welch to receive President's Medal |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubnow/stories/2016/04/commencement-awards.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=April 26, 2016}}</ref> He was named a Fellow of the [[National Academy of Inventors]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hsu |first1=Charlotte |title=Paras Prasad named Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors |url=http://engineering.buffalo.edu/home/news/research.host.html/content/shared/university/news/news-center-releases/2016/12/016.detail.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=December 13, 2016}}</ref> and earned the Gold Medal of the International Society for Optics and Photonics (SPIE).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hsu |first1=Charlotte |title=UB's Prasad receives SPIE Gold Medal |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubnow/stories/2016/03/prasad-spie-gold.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=March 14, 2016}}</ref> In 2017, he received the American Chemical Society [[Peter Debye Award]] in Physical Chemistry, IEEE Nanotechnology Council [[Pioneer Award in Nanotechnology]], and Michael S. Feld Biophotonics Award from [[Optica (society)|the Optical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hsu |first1=Charlotte |title=Prasad wins three national awards |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubnow/stories/2017/09/prasad-awards.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=September 25, 2017}}</ref>

In 2018, Prasad was elected a Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] for his contributions in biophotonics, nanophotonics and novel biomedical technology.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hsu |first1=Charlotte |title=Prasad selected IEEE fellow |url=http://engineering.buffalo.edu/ee/news-events/dept_news/paras-prasad-IEEE.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=January 5, 2018}}</ref> He was named to the clarivate Analytics 2018 Highly Cited Researchers list.<ref>{{cite web |title=Profs named to Highly Cited Researcher list |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubnow/briefs/2018/12/highly-cited-researchers.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=December 17, 2018}}</ref> In June 2021, Prasad received the IEEE Photonics Society William Streifer Scientific Achievement Award for "pioneering contributions in multiphoton processes in molecular materials and developing technologies that advance biophotonics for multiphoton imaging and therapy."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hsu |first1=Charlotte |title=UB's Paras Prasad receives prestigious IEEE award |url=http://engineering.buffalo.edu/ee/research/research_news/paras-prasad-ieee-award-2021.html |publisher=University at Buffalo |access-date=October 4, 2021 |date=June 29, 2021}}</ref>
